Fix the YIELD-WITHOUT-A-NAMED-WAIT fleet-stop and close the protocol gaps surfaced by production run 012-risk-ladder-actuation (mma-3), where executor-7 twice sent a courtesy status message to PM, ended its turn believing it was waiting, and parked indefinitely — no inbound signal was pending, so its persistent inbox never fired and the whole plan starved behind the final task. Core fix, protocol §3: the YIELD RULE — an agent may end a turn (outside task-complete/exit states) only with a named wait recorded, appending WAITING_ON (awaited signal + counterparty) or BLOCKED_ON (external condition, e.g. another task's file hold) as the last act before yielding; no nameable signal ⇒ keep calling tools. PM communication is clarified as two-way for PM-initiated status checks (always reply) but courtesy reports get no reply and are never grounds to end a turn. Detection ladder — script detects, PM verifies, Lead only on confirmed incidents: usage-monitor.sh check_silence now also emits a NUDGE candidate ({alert:NUDGE,task_id,silent_minutes,count}, all modes incl. push-through) only on the full conjunction silent>10min ∧ latest signal not WAITING_ON/BLOCKED_ON ∧ no repo file activity in 10min (find with .git + plan-dir pruned — the monitor's own trace writes must not count as work; the shared-tree imprecision is deliberate: a real fleet-stop quiets the whole tree, so the suppressor is weakest exactly when it matters least). PM verifies the candidate (re-read signals tail, own message history, optional pane liveness), pings the executor with a self-diagnosing status check (the ping itself cures a wrongly-parked live agent), and escalates NUDGE-ESCALATION to Lead only on count>=2 with no reply; Lead row added (verify, re-send/re-signal, or Phase 4 re-spawn). New signal vocabulary (§5, 20→23): WAITING_ON, BLOCKED_ON, PROGRESS (optional heartbeat before long no-write phases; resets the silence clock) — all three are state-only raw file appends exempt from the dual-write; §6 crash recovery gains a WAITING_ON/BLOCKED_ON row (verify the awaited item didn't arrive after the append before re-parking). Also closed from the same run: verdict-in-mailbox-but-not-in-signals (PM re-reads then nudges the author to append; signal_gap_nudge event), budget window-rollover blind spot (monitor tracks resets_at per window and appends a quiet usage_window_rolled event to events.json in all modes; PM sets cost_pct null for tasks spanning it instead of a negative value), and the impl.md audit race (CODE_COMPLETE means source done, NOT impl.md on disk — FILE-UPDATED task-N/impl.md is the report flag; protocol note). summary: Fix the Lead SendMessage address in plan-execution: task-team agents (and the never-resolved `{lead name}` placeholder in spawn prompts) addressed the Lead as `lead`, which the Claude Code harness rejects — the leader's harness-reserved recipient name is `team-lead`. Empirically verified on Claude Code v2.1.201 (tmux teammate mode) with a probe teammate: `to:"team-lead"` delivers to the main conversation (success + actual receipt), `to:"lead"` hard-fails (`success:false`, "No agent named 'lead' is reachable"), and `to:"main"` is a self-address the harness rejects for a NAMED teammate (only anonymous background subagents use `main`). Impact of the bug: every Executor→Lead message (`task done`, `code complete`, pipeline planning-complete, `QUERY`, `ADVICE REQUEST`, escalation, `PLAN-INVALIDATING`) silently failed to route — and since the Lead does not read task `signals.jsonl`, the signal-less ones were lost outright. Changes: `to:"lead"`→`to:"team-lead"` in agents/task-executor.md (3 sites); resolved `{lead name}`→`team-lead` in skills/plan-execution/references/phase-2-spawn-prompts.md (Executor/Reviewer/Tester/PM/final-gate teammate-list + Lead-name lines); documented `team-lead` as the canonical Lead address in execution-communication-protocol.md §1 as the single source of truth (with the `lead`/`main` rejections and the note that the `author:"lead"` log label is not an address). Also refreshed .claude/ultra/research/claude-code-sendmessage.md (was ~2 months stale) with current leader-addressing findings and issue statuses (#43706 background-teammate→lead, #42999 name-vs-ID partial fix v2.1.196, #25135 orphaned-inbox). Directionality note: teammates CAN originate SendMessage in this version and delivery to the correct name is reliable here, so no file-based Lead-inbox was needed — the fix is purely the correct address. Plugin-side files only — no project-level structure change.

Plan-execution wait mechanism: replace the per-signal bounded Monitor round with ONE persistent per-agent `tail -F` inbox monitor. execution-communication-protocol.md §3 fully rewritten: each task-team agent arms a single `tail -n +$((PROCESSED_LINES+1)) -F signals.jsonl | grep --line-buffered -E '"signal":"(<role-union>)"'` monitor once at startup (persistent: true), and every 'wait' becomes just 'yield your turn' — no per-wait monitor, no re-arm churn, and an agent blocked on two producers (review+test, or the two exit-confirms) is woken by that one inbox rather than two concurrent monitors. Detection is event-driven via the file-follow (~0 latency) and therefore covers SendMessage's documented silent-drop/orphaned-inbox bugs directly; a monotonic PROCESSED_LINES cursor (baked into the command, not a fresh wc -l) closes the arm/replay gap and de-dupes, and both verdicts are reset to pending on each fix so a stale prior-cycle PASS can't satisfy the gate. The per-agent recovery ladder (resend@12/escalate@24/hard-fail@40) is removed; with no per-agent timer, stall detection for a dead/stuck counterparty is delegated entirely to the PM's independent watch (scripts/usage-monitor.sh check_stalls, >10 min silence → STALL → Lead), and WAIT_TIMEOUT's writer changes from 'any waiter' to Lead (recorded when a PM STALL can't be resolved). §4/§5/§6 adjusted (telemetry drops `round`; §6 sets cursor to EOF and re-derives verdicts as latest-after-last-request; RESUME re-derives from signals.jsonl). Consumers synced by reference (task-team-startup.md gains an 'arm your inbox monitor' step; task-executor/code-review/task-tester get TaskStop teardown at exit + RESUME re-derive; SKILL.md Lead STALL handler is now the sole stall net and flags benign pipeline-parked-successor stalls; project-manager.md STALL section notes it is the sole stall net). Rethink the execution communication 'signals' layer — reframe + instrument, no behavioral removal. Motivated by the question of whether signals.jsonl is a redundant alternative to SendMessage that could be feature-flag-disabled. Research (see .claude/ultra/research/claude-code-sendmessage.md) showed the framing was wrong: the file does three jobs and only one overlaps with SendMessage — (1) crash recovery (a re-spawned agent reconstructs pipeline state; SendMessage has no message replay across a process death), (2) observer/audit state (PM stage-tracking and the operational-report timeline derive from it; SendMessage reaches only live recipients), and (3) a delivery backstop against Claude Code's documented, still-open name-addressing bugs (SendMessage(to: name) can return success yet never deliver — issue #42999, open; orphaned-inbox silent drop — #25135, won't-fix). This system addresses every teammate by name, so it is exposed to exactly those bugs; and the famous ~10-min stall was a foreground-wait posture bug (already fixed by bounded Monitor rounds), not a SendMessage drop. Conclusion: do NOT disable — measure whether the backstop ever fires, and correct the docs that mis-sell it as merely a SendMessage backup. Changes: (A) Reframe — execution-communication-protocol.md preamble now describes signals.jsonl as a durable, append-only shared state log (jobs 1-3) rather than a SendMessage backup; the §1 sender note, §3 opener, the CLAUDE.md Agent-Team Communication Protocol mandate (point 1), the Task Executor help entry, and docs/views/docs/plan-execution.ejs were updated to match (the docs Execution-communication section already named the SendMessage bugs). (B) Instrument — the PM operational report gains a Communication Channel Health section: deterministic, signals.jsonl-derived counts of resends (~12m, soft indicator), STALLED-WAIT escalations (~24m), and WAIT_TIMEOUT hard-fails (~40m) — the authoritative measure — plus best-effort backstop-save counts from a new per-task tasks/task-N/comms-telemetry.jsonl. The §3 wake checklist now appends one resolved_by (sendmessage|file) line per completed pure wait (additive, must never block). All counts ~0 across runs ⇒ the primary channel is healthy and the backstop near-vestigial; any non-zero ⇒ it earned its keep. (C) Cadence audit/tune (the perceived 'spam' is idle agents waking every ~4 min during pure waits): the pure-wait Monitor round cap is 240s→300s and the inner poll is sleep 5s→10s; the recovery ladder is re-keyed to elapsed-wait minutes (~12/24/40) instead of raw round counts so lengthening a round can't silently delay escalation; usage-monitor.sh poll is 60s→120s (it is silent on clean ticks, so this is churn/debug-log reduction, not output-rate — and it is symlinked into ~/.claude/ultra, so the change propagates on plugin update with no /uc:setup re-run). Round length only bounds the rarely-used backstop wake; SendMessage wakes immediately on the happy path, so a longer round costs nothing when delivery works. Deferred to a data-gated follow-up (explicitly NOT in this change): a kill-switch flag, a graduated full|lean comms flag, and the root-cause addressing fix (agent-ID addressing / a name→ID hook) plus refreshing the expired SendMessage research. Help skill and docs site synced.

Add tmux window naming. New shipped primitive scripts/tmux-window-name.sh renames the current tmux WINDOW (the window-name analogue of tmux-layout-setup.sh, which manages pane labels; the two are orthogonal — the layout daemon never touches window names). It owns the single $TMUX_PANE runtime gate, sanitizes the requested name (collapses whitespace, keeps the '::' delimiter unambiguous, lone colons -> '-'), truncates to ~40 chars for the status bar, renames the window, and disables tmux automatic-rename/allow-rename so the shell prompt or programs don't overwrite it; logs to ~/.claude/ultra/tmux-window-name.log and always exits 0 so it can never break a caller; no-ops outside tmux. New user-invocable skill /uc:rename-window wraps it for manual renames and documents the convention. Standardized naming wired into the planning/execution flows: each mode names its window on entry (UC::Feature::<subject>, UC::Debug::<subject>, UC::Discovery::<subject>, UC::Roadmap::<scope>); the shared planning-framework Stage 4 (new Step 5d) upgrades feature/debug windows to the plan form UC::P-NNN::<README title> once the plan is written; and plan-execution Phase 1 (new §1.1c) names the window UC::P-NNN::<README title> right after the existing layout setup. Redesign plan-execution usage monitoring to stop nudging the Lead. The old chain (Haiku watchdog -> PM -> Lead) emitted non-actionable signals (recurring STATUS, advisory CONSERVE, stale-data) that woke the Opus Lead for nothing, on top of the unavoidable agent-team idle/lifecycle notifications. Verified against the official agent-teams docs (v2.1.178): the lead is always auto-notified when a teammate goes idle and on every teammate message, with no suppression and no nested teams — so the fix is to reduce wake frequency and silence residual wakes, not to deafen the Lead. Changes: (1) New shipped script scripts/usage-monitor.sh — the single source of truth for usage (account resolution + thresholds in ONE place, ending the wrong-account class of bug). Two subcommands: `watch` (persistent, run by PM via the Monitor tool; emits ONLY on the critical-stop crossing, the work-can-restart reset incl. the seq-178 time-authoritative reset, and stalls; carries the reset_latch logic) and `status` (one-shot JSON: both windows + a clear/soft/critical band). (2) Deleted the Watchdog agent (agents/watchdog.md) and collapsed it into PM — PM owns the monitor, removing the relay hop and one teammate that idle-nudged the Lead. PM applies the chosen usage mode and forwards to the Lead ONLY actionable events (USAGE STOP / USAGE RESET / STALL). (3) The usage mode (push-through vs auto-pause, mapping to extra_usage) is now the FIRST user interaction of plan-execution (phase-1-setup 1.0b), sourced from `usage-monitor.sh status`; set once, never re-asked; removes the first-tick STATUS dependency. (4) The soft limit is no longer an interrupt — the Lead enforces it with a pre-spawn `status` check (don't start new work while soft); the script never emits for it. In push-through mode usage emits are suppressed entirely. (5) Removed the Lead 'wake-up trace' diagnostic so unavoidable residual auto-wakes are silent. Also removed the watchdog pane from the tmux layout daemon (scripts/tmux-layout-daemon.js) and reclaimed its space for the Lead/main pane (left-column weights pm 30 / main 70, was watchdog 20 / pm 30 / main 50). Reliability hardening so the Lead can't fabricate a usage status (observed: a Lead narrating an invented limit state): usage-monitor.sh is invoked via the stable absolute path ~/.claude/ultra/usage-monitor.sh (symlinked by /uc:setup alongside lib.sh/statusline; self-healed in phase-1 preflight) instead of $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, which is frequently unset in a Bash shell; verified the path resolves account + bands with CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT explicitly unset. Lead and PM now carry an explicit anti-fabrication rule (only act on/forward usage figures that came from the script's actual stdout; if it errors, stop and surface — never guess), and phase-1 verifies the script runs before relying on it. Made `status` mode time-authoritative too (it previously only lived in `watch`): usage-status.json can hold a STALE percentage whose reset time has already passed (statusline rewrites updated_at every refresh even when the rate-limit numbers are not, so a window can read 101% minutes after it rolled over and updated_at can't detect it). status now treats any window whose resets_at has passed as `clear` (band + a `reset_elapsed` flag), so a pre-spawn check or up-front read no longer gates `critical` on a stale post-reset number; `stale_minutes` is kept for visibility but documented as unreliable. Existing installs should re-run /uc:setup to create the new symlink. Scope: usage-monitoring chain only (per-task idle churn untouched). New unit test scripts/tests/test-usage-monitor.sh (16 checks). Help skill + docs site (token-efficiency, plan-execution, reference) synced.

Fix plan-execution never auto-resuming after a usage-window reset (paused overnight, required a manual morning restart). Two root causes. (1) The watchdog could never detect a reset while paused: its bash script reads usage from ~/.claude/ultra/usage-status.json, which is only refreshed by statusline.sh on a new API response — but a PAUSE makes every agent idle, so zero API calls happen and the file goes stale forever. The time-based reset check (now > resets_at) was gated behind the (stale) percentage first dropping below CONSERVE, so it was structurally unreachable; the watchdog ticked every 60s but never emitted USAGE-RESET. Fix A (agents/watchdog.md): make reset detection time-authoritative — when a window previously alerted and its known resets_at has passed, emit USAGE-RESET regardless of the (possibly stale) percentage (carrying reason:reset_time_passed), guarded by resets_at>0. A per-window reset_latch (added to .watchdog-state.json init, read with jq // 0 so old state files still work) suppresses re-alerting on the same stale data until resets_at advances after work resumes, preventing an immediate spurious re-PAUSE. PM (agents/project-manager.md) now interprets the reset_time_passed variant so it doesn't report the stale pct as current usage. (2) The Lead's only wake path was watchdog→PM→Lead, which silently broke. Fix B (skills/plan-execution/SKILL.md + references/usage-control.md): per the user's principle 'pause is allowed, abandoning is not', the Lead now arms a self-owned one-shot HOLD-WAKE Monitor at the known reset time when entering hold state — a guaranteed self-restart independent of the watchdog/PM chain — and may only go idle once that wake is armed and the watchdog is confirmed alive; otherwise it surfaces to the user instead of going silent. HOLD-WAKE and the watchdog's USAGE-RESET are two independent, idempotent triggers for the same recovery. The old 'Lead does NOT need its own cron during pause' guidance is reversed. Watchdog check_window logic verified with 13 scenario unit tests. Help skill and docs site (token-efficiency, plan-execution, reference) synced.

Make plan-execution spawn real tmux team members and cancel if it can't. The seq-176 fix corrected the teammate spawn tool name (TeamCreate → Agent) but never addressed the teammate execution BACKEND. Verified against the installed Claude Code 2.1.179 binary: how a named teammate runs is governed by the `teammateMode` settings.json key (tmux | in-process | auto), resolved per session — the Agent tool has no per-call override — and a BackendRegistry silently falls back to `in-process` when the mode resolves to in-process, the session is non-interactive, or no pane backend is reachable. With `teammateMode` unset (the machine default), named teammates spawn in-process with NO tmux panes, silently breaking the pane-based coordination plan-execution depends on (the reported 'it didn't run as a team / no panes' failure). Confirmed live: a named spawn created no pane and the session team config recorded every member as backendType=in-process, vs an older team that recorded backendType=tmux + a real tmuxPaneId. Fix: (1) /uc:setup now configures `teammateMode` in ~/.claude/settings.json (recommended `tmux`; avoids `auto` because it silently degrades), with a check (§3.2b) and fix (§5.2b) and a new marker field; (2) plan-execution gains a two-layer backend gate — a pre-spawn heuristic in phase-1-setup §1.0 (require $TMUX set AND teammateMode=tmux, else STOP) and an authoritative post-spawn check in §1.9 that reads the team config's backendType and ABORTS the run (shutdown_request to PM/watchdog) if any teammate is in-process, instead of running the degraded pipeline; prerequisite #3 changed from 'tmux optional' to 'tmux required'. (3) Spawn prompts now pass `subagent_type` as the registered type name (uc:Task Executor, etc.) instead of a file path, and the final-gate tester gets an explicit name (tester-final-gate). Docs site, help skill, and versioning synced. Existing users must re-run `/uc:setup` and relaunch inside tmux to pick up `teammateMode`.

Fix the intermittent plan-execution failure where the Lead announces the agent-teams tools aren't available and silently degrades to a lossy one-shot subagent pipeline (dropping PM, watchdog, peer messaging, signal durability, and pipeline pre-spawn). Root cause: the skill instructed the Lead to spawn teammates with a tool named `TeamCreate` (and `team_name`) and one-shot research via the 'Task tool' — neither name exists in current Claude Code. Verified against the live `Agent` tool schema (its `team_name` param is now 'Deprecated; ignored. The session has a single implicit team', and `name` 'makes it addressable via SendMessage') and ToolSearch (no TeamCreate/TeamAdd/CreateTeam tool): teammates are spawned via the `Agent` tool in teammate mode (`name` + `run_in_background: true`); one-shot subagents via the `Agent` tool foreground with no name. The teammate↔subagent distinction is unchanged and still load-bearing — only the obsolete tool name is corrected. Adds phase-1-setup §1.0 Lead Tooling Preflight: load the deferred agent-teams tools via `ToolSearch(select:SendMessage,Monitor,TaskCreate,TaskUpdate,TaskList)`, an availability gate that STOPS with a `/uc:setup` instruction if SendMessage is unavailable (replacing the invented degradation), and an explicit primitive mapping. Clarifies that `CommunicateTeamMember`/`CommunicateTeam`/`WaitForTeamMember` are protocol PROCEDURES (SendMessage + signals.jsonl + Monitor), not tools — added a banner to execution-communication-protocol.md and reinforced in SKILL.md. Replaced all TeamCreate/'Task tool' references across plan-execution SKILL.md + phase-1/phase-2 references, research and discovery-mode skills, and the docs site (plan-execution.ejs, token-efficiency.ejs). `shutdown_request` left as-is (out of scope).

Extract tmux layout setup into a single always-invoked script (scripts/tmux-layout-setup.sh) instead of inline conditional bash the Lead model had to interpret. plan-execution phase-1 §1.1b and phase-2 §2.6 now just `bash ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/tmux-layout-setup.sh` — the script owns the conditions, so the model instruction is trivial and hard to skip/paraphrase wrong. The script's single runtime gate is `$TMUX_PANE`, matching the design already documented in setup/references/tmux-modes.md ("$TMUX_PANE is the runtime signal … the setup-time tmuxMode preference does not matter at runtime"); the old inline block's extra `TMUX_MODE != none/custom` check was inconsistent with that and is dropped — in tmux ⇒ name the pane, full stop. Effects unchanged and idempotent: ensure the daemon, label the current pane @agent-name=main-context, enable the pane-border label display. Adds full action/skip logging to ~/.claude/ultra/tmux-layout-setup.log (1 MB cap) for future debugging. Complements the daemon self-heal (seq 174): the script makes the common case deterministic, the daemon infers the Lead pane if the label is ever still missing.

Tmux layout daemon self-heals the Lead/main pane label instead of depending on a model-driven tmux step. Root cause of recurring 'window never arranged' reports: the `main-context` label is set by an instruction the Lead model has to choose to run (phase-1 §1.1b / phase-2 §2.6), and it gets skipped when /uc:plan-execution is invoked mid-session — leaving the Lead pane unlabelled, which made the daemon skip the entire window (teammate panes piled up un-gridded; the window never appeared in the daemon log). Teammates self-label mechanically, so the fix is inference: classifyPanes now promotes the lone unlabelled pane in a window that already has PM/watchdog/task panes to main-context, and tick() persists that label once via set-option (so the border is correct and later ticks classify it directly). The daemon no longer depends on the Lead ever running a label command; §1.1b/§2.6 remain as belt-and-suspenders for the border before the first arrange. Likely external trigger for the recent recurrence: a Claude Code update (2.1.177, installed two days prior) changing agent-teams pane spawning — the daemon fix is robust to that regardless.

Tmux layout daemon: the Lead's main pane is now reliably labelled `main-context`, so the daemon never skips a live execution window. Root cause: the daemon only manages a window once its Lead pane carries `@agent-name=main-context`, but that label was set in exactly one place — a one-shot in phase-1-setup §1.1b. If the Lead's controlling pane differed from `$TMUX_PANE` at startup, or the Lead moved to a new window after §1.1b ran, the label never landed on the pane the teammates spawned beside; the daemon then ignored the whole window (teammate panes piled up un-gridded, zero log lines for that window). Fix: re-assert the same idempotent label in Phase 2's Pre-Spawn Checklist (new §2.6), which runs before EVERY TeamCreate (initial spawn AND pipeline pre-spawn) — so the main pane is guaranteed labelled before the first teammate pane appears. Same mode gating as §1.1b (skipped for tmux mode none/custom or when $TMUX_PANE is unset). §1.1b cross-references §2.6 as the durable re-assertion. Verified swap-pane preserves pane-scoped @agent-name (keyed to pane_id), so the daemon's reordering is not the cause.

New Project Manager startup step 7 detects connection (both `.claude/ultra/project-id` present AND `ultraclaude-agent status` confirming the daemon is live), resolves the host from `~/.claude/ultra/agent/<host>/config.json` (default dashboard.ultra-claude.dev), and sends Lead `Dashboard live at https://{host}/projects/{project-id}` — otherwise it sends nothing (no placeholder, no block). Tmux layout daemon: dedup panes by pane_id per window in scanPanes(). `tmux list-panes -a` enumerates a window once per session it belongs to, so a window shared across a session GROUP (e.g. VS Code's tmux integration, where `vscode`/`vscode-37` share windows) lists every pane once per grouped session. The duplicate rows inflated the current pane count past the target — the scalar role slots (main/pm/watchdog/gate) collapse via last-wins while task/unnamed arrays keep duplicates, producing a stable current = target + (singleton roles present) mismatch — so arrangeWindow aborted with a pane-count-mismatch on every tick and never applied a layout. The manager was effectively non-functional for any window living in a grouped session. Fixed by skipping already-seen pane_ids per window during the scan.

Execution communication protocol: pure waits become bounded Monitor rounds (~4 min) with a recovery ladder (resend ~12m, escalate to Lead ~24m, visible WAIT_TIMEOUT hard-fail ~40m; SHUTDOWN/RESUME waits exempt). Fixes the production failure where an unbounded foreground until-loop blocked the agent's turn and starved SendMessage delivery (the backup channel silenced the primary one, e.g. a ~10-min ADVICE_RESPONSE stall). SendMessage stays the primary channel; signals.jsonl stays the durable backup. Monitor tool added to Task Executor, Code Reviewer, and Task Tester frontmatter. Add SendMessage to tool lists of all pipeline agents that coordinate via messages: task-executor (19 body refs), project-manager (10), code-review (4), task-tester (4). Watchdog first-tick STATUS report replaces Lead's direct usage file read. The script now emits {"alert":"STATUS","pct_5h":...,"pct_7d":...} on its first tick, PM forwards to Lead, and Lead waits for this before spawning task teams. Eliminates Lead reading usage-status.json directly (which could hit stale data from idle sessions). Watchdog is now the single source of truth for all usage data. Updated PM, phase-1-setup, spawn prompts, and usage-control reference.

Watchdog script outputs JSON lines instead of plain text. Fixes hallucination bug where Haiku fabricated alerts from Monitor lifecycle notifications (e.g. inventing 'KILL 5h 100' when usage was 4%). Script now emits structured JSON like {"alert":"KILL","window":"5h","pct":96,"resets_at":...} — Haiku checks for JSON with an "alert" field and ignores anything else. Also: added SendMessage to watchdog tool list (was missing — the agent couldn't forward alerts), added debug log (.watchdog-debug.log) that records every tick's readings and account key, simplified check_window with rank-based tier comparison replacing duplicated escalation logic. Updated PM agent and spawn prompts to parse the new JSON format.

Fix Watchdog monitoring wrong account in multi-account setups. The bash script used '.accounts | sort_by(.updated_at) | last' which picked whichever account was most recently written to, not the one running the plan. Now Lead resolves the active account key via 'claude auth status' + slugifyEmail at plan start (new step 1.8), passes ACCOUNT_KEY through the watchdog spawn prompt, and the script uses '.accounts[$key]' for direct lookup. Same fix applied to the pre-task budget assessment and usage-control reference.

Replace CronCreate with Monitor in the Watchdog agent. A self-contained bash monitoring script now does all threshold checking (CONSERVE/PAUSE/KILL for both 5h and 7d windows), stall detection, and data freshness — running every 60 seconds in a persistent Monitor process. The script outputs alert lines ONLY on state transitions; clean ticks produce zero stdout. Monitor delivers each line as a notification to the Haiku model, which simply forwards it to PM via SendMessage. On clean ticks: no stdout → no Monitor notification → model never prompted → zero tokens wasted → zero Lead noise. Previously, CronCreate fired a prompt every minute forcing the model to respond (framework constraint: models can't produce zero tokens), and TeamCreate delivered the response to Lead, burning ~30-60K Opus tokens per 5-hour execution for nothing. The bash script handles: per-window threshold evaluation with escalation (CONSERVE→PAUSE→KILL), USAGE-RESET detection, state file management (.watchdog-state.json), data freshness checks with 10-minute cooldown, stall detection against events.json/plan.json, and stall-ping cleanup for completed tasks.

Remove error logging, incident reports, and user escalation from chrome-debug skill. Step 8 (log incident if unresolved) removed entirely. PM communication section removed. Replace two-tier usage control (SOFT-LIMIT/HARD-LIMIT) with three-tier CONSERVE/PAUSE/KILL system. CONSERVE (5h ≥80%, 7d ≥90%) stops spawning new teams — no agent messages sent. PAUSE (5h ≥90%, 7d ≥95%) tells all active agents to go idle via text message — idle agents consume zero tokens, full context preserved. KILL (5h ≥95%, 7d ≥98%) force-terminates agents via shutdown_request protocol message — the only mechanism that reliably stops agents. On USAGE RESET: PAUSE recovery sends RESUME to idle agents (instant, zero re-spawn cost); KILL recovery re-spawns teams from checkpoint using per-task files (crash-recovery flow). Lead enters hold state during PAUSE/KILL — defers all ADVICE/QUERY from paused/killed agents to prevent accidentally unblocking stopped work. Watchdog signals renamed throughout (CONSERVE/PAUSE/KILL replace SOFT-LIMIT/HARD-LIMIT). PM forwarding updated to match. Fold the tmux disconnected-session reaper (formerly /uc:session-cleanup) into /uc:setup as an optional, strictly opt-in step backed by a new reference file at skills/setup/references/session-cleanup.md. The opt-in prompt in the reference spells out that the reaper CLEANS UP stale tmux sessions but DISRUPTS the ability to resume any detached session older than 24 hours (scrollback and running processes are lost) — users who rely on long-lived detached tmux sessions are told to skip. Remove the original Ultra session-file cleanup sub-flow from /uc:session-cleanup. The skill is now exclusively the tmux disconnected-session reaper installer from seq 135 — no more Step 0 AskUserQuestion with two paths, no more transcript index, no more `.claude/ultra/sessions/*.json` walking or classification. The file-based method was never reliable in practice: the Ultra session file schema has no `pid`, no `last_activity`, and no tmux linkage, and cross-referencing Claude Code transcript jsonl files for liveness proved fragile (dash-as-slash encoding collisions, bind-mount duplicates, stuck-active files that outlived the transcripts). Keeping the tmux reaper as the only method — it has a precise liveness signal (`session_last_attached` + `session_created` from tmux format vars), runs out-of-band via a user-level systemd timer, and solves the actual pain point for VSCode Remote SSH users. The help skill entry and docs/views/docs/reference.ejs row are updated to describe the single remaining sub-flow. A short note in the skill's Notes section acknowledges the removed session-file method so users re-reading the skill understand why it's gone. The skill frontmatter is tightened: Glob/Grep dropped from allowed-tools (no longer walks projects), argument-hint clarifies the install/repair/remove decision tree. No project-template files change — the skill only writes under $HOME — so migration is null.

Extend the session-cleanup skill with a second sub-flow: an optional tmux disconnected-session reaper for Linux/systemd users. The original Ultra session-file cleanup becomes sub-flow A; the new sub-flow B detects install state, describes the proposed behavior to the user (including a live dump of current tmux sessions and which ones would be killed right now), and on confirmation installs three files — `$HOME/.local/bin/tmux-reap-disconnected.sh`, `$HOME/.config/systemd/user/tmux-reap.service`, and `$HOME/.config/systemd/user/tmux-reap.timer` — then enables the user-level timer and verifies it is active. The reaper uses `session_last_attached` and `session_created` from tmux format vars to compute per-session disconnect age, kills anything detached for more than 24h, and never touches currently-attached sessions. Motivating scenario: VSCode Remote SSH users whose integrated terminals auto-launch tmux end up with tmux sessions piling up on the VM after every window close — this gives them a hands-off, threshold-based cleanup without resorting to `destroy-unattached on` (which wrongly kills sessions on manual Ctrl-b d) or CPU-idle heuristics (which can't distinguish afk-with-claude-code from truly dead). The sub-flow also handles loginctl linger (required so the timer runs when no SSH session is active) and offers repair/reinstall/remove paths for idempotency. Non-Linux platforms skip sub-flow B cleanly. Step 0 now asks which sub-flow(s) to run via AskUserQuestion, so existing callers of the skill that only want session-file cleanup still get it in one click. Help skill entry updated to describe both sub-flows. No project-template files change — the skill installs machine-local systemd units under `$HOME`, not under any project — so migration is null.

Cut idle Watchdog and PM wake-ups to Lead at the source. The Lead wake-up trace from seq 132 immediately caught three noise wake-ups in a single screenshot: two from Watchdog ('task verification — initialized, no alerts' and 'no action needed') and one from PM ('PM ready, plan.json healthy'). None carry actionable content. Watchdog is a Haiku cron agent previously instructed to 'respond with just ok' on clean ticks; that 'ok' text — plus any improvised status word Haiku produces — was leaking to the spawner (Lead) as assistant-turn output, and the stylistic 'Do not message Lead' rule was too weak to stop improvisation. PM was emitting one informational startup ping ('PM initialized — plan.json and events.json ready. Monitoring active.') that Lead has no handler for and never acts on. Edits in agents/watchdog.md: the CronCreate TICK prompt (step 3), the Monitoring Checks preamble, section 4 'Respond', and the 'What NOT to do' list now all require silent turns on clean ticks — no text, no SendMessage, just end the turn. The Lead rule is strengthened from 'Do not message Lead' to 'NEVER SendMessage to Lead under any circumstances; the ONLY allowed recipient is pm-{PLAN_NAME}; even on shutdown you reply in-thread, you do not initiate.' This makes the rule mechanical (single-recipient constraint) instead of stylistic, which Haiku follows better. Edits in agents/project-manager.md: the startup SendMessage to Lead is removed from the startup sequence (step 7) and its mirror bullet is removed from PM's 'You send to Lead' documentation list, so the spec matches the behavior. All validated alert paths stay untouched — PM still forwards USAGE HARD/SOFT-LIMIT, USAGE RESET, STALL, STALE DATA, dashboard URL, escalations, and the operational-report notice, all of which are actionable with matching handler rows in plan-execution. The wake-up trace itself is deliberately kept in place so the user can verify the noise is gone before removing the audit tool; a future plan will remove the trace once silence is confirmed. No project-template files change, so migration is null.

Rewrite /uc:session-cleanup around the actual schema the session-start/session-end hooks produce. Previous version classified by `pid`, `last_activity`, and `tmux_pane` — fields that were documented but never written by any hook, so classification silently defaulted every real file to ENDED/LEGACY and the stuck-active bucket was invisible. Also fixed a lossy project-discovery bug: decoding `~/.claude/projects/` directory names by replacing every dash with a slash drops every project whose name contains a hyphen, so large project trees were missed entirely. The new flow: (1) walk the filesystem with `find $HOME -path '*/.claude/ultra/sessions'` instead of decoding encoded names; (2) build a `session_id → transcript_mtime` index from `$HOME/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl` because Claude Code's transcript is the only file that gets appended on every turn — the Ultra session.json is written once at start and once at end, so it is useless as a liveness signal; (3) classify each session file using `started_at` age + transcript-mtime silence against a single user-supplied threshold (default 1 day): young sessions are always kept, old sessions are killed unless their transcript was touched within the threshold, legacy sessions (no `started_at`) are killed unless transcript-active; (4) present a per-project kill plan and delete via a simple `rm` stream over a temp kill-list file. Added a Background section explaining the real schema so future readers don't rebuild the same wrong mental model. Tmux-pane killing removed — the schema never carried a tmux reference. help/SKILL.md entry rewritten to match. Also removes 7 session-state files that had been accidentally tracked in this repo before `.gitignore` started excluding `.claude/ultra/sessions/`.

Plan-execution Lead: replace the 'be silent between messages' rule with a temporary wake-up trace requirement so the user can audit which senders are actually noisy. Background: Lead has been spamming 'Waiting for executor-N' / state-narration text between handler turns. Root cause is structural — Claude's assistant loop must produce either a tool call or text per turn, and rows like FILE-UPDATED ('No Lead action') and pipeline 'planning complete — awaiting implementation approval' ('No reply needed') give Lead nothing to call, so the model fills the empty turn with narration. Prose telling it to 'be silent' can't beat the mechanical constraint. Interim diagnostic fix: every wake-up must produce exactly one sentence describing the message just received (sender + type + task ID), e.g. 'Received: FILE-UPDATED task-3/impl.md from executor-3.' or 'Received: code complete from executor-2.' This is the only allowed per-wake-up text — no commentary, no prediction, no 'waiting for X.' Once the user has reviewed the trace logs, we'll cut the noisy senders at the source (likely: stop CC'ing Lead on FILE-UPDATED broadcasts, drop the pipeline parking confirmation ping) and remove the trace requirement. Edits in skills/plan-execution/SKILL.md: rewrote the Message Handlers preamble (line 113), updated the post-handler return rule (line 138), expanded the Anti-Patterns section to clarify that the trace is the only allowed output and is not a license for narration, and tightened the constraint bullet.

Consolidate Tech Stack sweep rule into the planning framework base (follow-up to seq 130). The previous commit put the mandatory sweep in references/planning-framework/stage-2.md AND duplicated mode-specific expansions in feature-mode and debug-mode stage-2.md — redundant restatements that would drift from the base rule over time. Consolidation: (1) base rule in planning-framework/stage-2.md rewritten to be fully mode-agnostic — 'Every planning mode ... must sweep /uc:research over every core technology the in-scope files will touch,' with the in-scope file set defined as 'whatever the active mode flags as in-scope for this planning session.' (2) mode extensions in feature-mode, debug-mode, and doc-code-verification-mode stage-2.md reduced to one-paragraph notes that name each mode's in-scope file source: feature = draft task breakdown's Files list; debug = files under investigation for the bug; verification = code files in the verification matrix. The mechanical sweep rule, strict derivation, canonicalization note, research-to-task mapping, and downstream effect all live in the base and are inherited by all modes. (3) doc-code-verification-mode gains its Tech Stack sweep note for the first time (wasn't in seq 130).

/uc:research gains canonical slug normalization + pre-flight duplicate prevention, and planning Stage 2 gains a mandatory Tech Stack sweep rule. Closes a regression vs. the old Tech Knowledge agent: when a plan 'just extended existing code using already-known libraries,' the new lazy research flow produced nothing because nothing was new — but the knowledge base also stayed empty, so executors and reviewers still hit cold QUERY round-trips for every library the codebase already uses. Two coordinated changes: (1) In SKILL.md Step 3, a new three-part flow — 3a derives a raw slug from the topic, 3b canonicalizes it by stripping version markers (`v\d+`, `\d+\.\d+`), topic-noise words (api/schema/config/middleware/client/consumer/etc. for library mode, strategies/patterns/approach for patterns mode, competitors/alternatives/trends for market mode), and method-level qualifiers, reducing 'nats jetstream consumer config' → `nats`, 'zod v4 schemas' → `zod`, 'prisma findUnique' → `prisma`. 3c runs a broader pre-flight jq query that matches existing entries whose subject is equal to or a whole-token prefix of the canonical slug (with `sort_by(subject | length)` preferring the shortest canonical home), so different phrasings of the same library always route to the same research file — no duplicates. (2) SKILL.md Step 1 gains a `--fill-only` flag: full flow still runs (classify → canonicalize → cache check → spawn on miss), but the caller's return payload is a compact `{target_path, mode, subject, status: hit|spawned|refreshed|failed, expires}` envelope instead of the H2 section content or agent summary. Designed for bulk sweeps where the caller only needs 'is this research on disk now?' not 'what does it say?' — saves ~2-5K tokens per entry. (3) New 'Tech Stack Sweep — MANDATORY' section in references/planning-framework/stage-2.md with a strict mechanical derivation rule: for every file in the draft Files list, read imports, sweep `/uc:research {lib} --fill-only` per external package. Applies even to libraries the project already uses — the whole point is to fill the knowledge base so execution teams get cache hits instead of cold QUERYs. (4) feature-mode and debug-mode Stage 2 extensions describe how each mode derives its file set for the sweep: feature-mode from the draft task breakdown, debug-mode from the files under investigation for the bug. Research-to-task mapping is tracked during Stage 2 and turned into task.md `**Research:**` pointers at Stage 4 Step 5b, with Lead's pre-spawn coverage check degrading to a rarely-firing safety net because the knowledge base is already populated.

/uc:research: fix silent cache-miss bailouts. The skill had conditional language in Step 6 ('If the index query returned null...') and no top-level invariant enforcing that every invocation produces a result. Agents running the skill could hit ambiguous in-between cases — index returned a fresh-by-date entry whose topics[] didn't actually cover the user's topic, or a weak summary-only match, or classification ambiguity that resolved to 'idk' — and silently return 'no match found' without firing Step 6. Fix: (1) new mandatory Invariant section at the top stating every invocation ends in one of two outcomes — cache hit or agent spawn, no third option; (2) rewrite Step 5 as an explicit three-check list (non-null entry AND topics/subject substring match AND not expired) with explicit fall-through to Step 6 on any miss, including H2-section-not-found-in-file (index claimed coverage the file doesn't deliver); (3) rewrite Step 6 header as 'MANDATORY ON ANY NON-HIT' with an enumerated list of cases that land there; (4) add 'cache miss is the default fallback, not a separate condition' guideline. No behavior change on successful cache hits; the fix closes the 'I checked the cache and nothing was a good match' failure mode where the agent would narrate instead of spawn.

Usage-limit management redesign: replace PM's 5-min cron polling with a three-agent system (Haiku watchdog → PM → Lead). New Haiku watchdog agent ticks every 1 minute checking usage thresholds (75% soft, 90% hard) and executor staleness (>10 min silence), signals PM only when something needs attention. PM becomes event-driven (no cron) — validates watchdog alerts, adds operational context, forwards to Lead with recommendations, tracks per-task budget data (usage % at start/end of each task). Lead is the decision-maker — can decide not to start task 1, stop spawning, pause teams, hard-stop, or resume, guided by new usage-control.md reference. Watchdog placed in PM column in tmux layout. Per-task budget object added to plan.json schema. ~6x token cost reduction for monitoring.

/uc:research splits cache into two scopes. Product/domain research stays at `documentation/technology/research/` (libraries, patterns) + `documentation/product/research/` (market). Rationale: Claude knowledge is meta — about the tooling we build *with*, not about the product domain — so it belongs alongside other harness state in `.claude/ultra/`, not under `documentation/technology/research/libraries/` (which implies importable libraries the product depends on). Skill auto-detects Claude/Anthropic topics in Step 2 and routes Step 3 (target path) and Step 4 (index path) to the harness scope. The researcher agent gained scope-aware bootstrap (creates `.claude/ultra/research/` with README + empty index on first Claude lookup), scope-aware index key format (flat for harness, relative-from-research-root for product), and an explicit `rm -f {index_path}.tmp` step in the atomic-write protocol to fix a tmp-file leak observed in testing. library-mode reference notes the dedicated output path; help skill description updated.

Reviewer speaks first: synthesizes a `REVIEWER TAKE` from task.md + standards + architecture and sends to Executor BEFORE plan.md is written, replacing the old advisory plan-review round-trip. Executor's plan.md becomes a thin execution delta (no restating task.md content); Executor runs a deviation self-check before implementing. Universal Lead plan-review gate removed — replaced by ADVICE channel with four cases (complicated / deep-reasoning / knowledge / deviation). actions: For each plan in documentation/plans/ that has a README.md containing `### Task N:` headings with embedded per-task fields (Description, Product context, Files, Patterns, Success criteria, Dependencies), split each task section out into `documentation/plans/{plan}/tasks/task-N/task.md` using `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/templates/task.md` as the template. Rewrite the README to contain only plan-level content + a flat task heading index (`### Task N: {Title} <!-- status:pending -->` followed by `- [ ] **Complete**`).

For each newly-created task.md, populate the **Research:** section by scanning the plan's old Tech Stack list and mapping each entry to `documentation/technology/research/libraries/{lib}.md` if that file exists. If the research file doesn't exist, write `None applicable` — Lead's pre-spawn knowledge review will fill real gaps at execution time via `/uc:research`.
Skip plans where `tasks/task-N/task.md` already exists — migration is idempotent.

If a legacy `shared/knowledge-brief.md` exists in any plan, leave it on disk as an inert historical artifact. Plan execution no longer reads it; per-task `task.md` Research sections are authoritative.

Completed plans (with operational-report.md or plan.json status `completed`) are safe to migrate — they just get a cleaner structure. In-progress plans will pick up the new structure automatically on their next `/uc:plan-execution` resume via the legacy-plan self-heal in phase-1-setup §1.1.
If you prefer not to migrate, `/uc:plan-execution` will self-heal each plan on resume — but migrating ahead of time keeps the git history cleaner and avoids mixed formats.
migration.conflicts: Projects with hand-customized plan README task sections (e.g., extra fields, non-standard markdown structure) may need manual review when splitting. The migration preserves all field content — the risk is only at the parsing boundary. If a plan has unusually-formatted task sections, extract them by hand. summary: /uc:research now handles Claude Code / Claude Agent SDK / Anthropic API questions natively. The library-mode reference now instructs the researcher to query Ref.tools AND fetch the curated `docs.claude.com` URL roots (`/en/docs/claude-code/`, `/en/api/`, `/en/api/agent-sdk/`) in parallel via WebSearch+WebFetch, merge both, and surface any discrepancies. A machine-maintained `index.json` (written atomically by the researcher, queried via jq by the skill) drives fast cache-hit lookups with zero agent spawn on hits. /uc:chrome-debug gains a multi-account failure mode: browser/Claude Code account mismatch. The bridge (wss://bridge.claudeusercontent.com) pairs Claude Code and the Claude-in-Chrome extension by matching Anthropic account identities on both ends — when Claude Code is authenticated as account X but the browser is logged into account Y, pairing silently fails and symptoms look like transport-layer problems (empty tabs_context_mcp, intermittent timeouts) that no amount of native-host restarting will fix. /uc:setup now checks whether the `ultraclaude-agent` npm package is installed and, if so, compares the installed version against the latest published on npm. When outdated, setup surfaces the gap in its status table and offers to run `npm update -g ultraclaude-agent` as part of the fix-missing-prerequisites flow (step 5.9). Never auto-installs the agent — installation remains a deliberate user choice. This closes a gap where users who installed the agent once and never ran `npm update` would miss every subsequent bug fix (including the project-path-with-spaces fix that blocks project discovery for any path containing a space). The npm lookup uses a 5-second timeout so offline/slow registries never stall setup. Marker file `~/.claude/ultra/uc-setup.json` now records the installed agent version (or null). Docs site `docs/views/docs/setup.ejs` mentions the new behavior. Help skill entry for /uc:setup updated with the new sentence.

Project Manager: explicit Lead label sanity check on every verification pass. PM now counts how many panes in the window carry `main-context` via `grep -cx`, interprets the count (1=healthy, 0=broken, 2+=duplicate), and self-heals the 0-case by relabeling the Lead pane back to the canonical `main-context`. Catches downstream drift where a project customization writes a non-canonical label like `lead-*` — the tmux layout daemon only anchors windows on `main-context`, so a wrong label silently stops the team grid from updating. PM also logs the incident in its operational report so the Lead can investigate where the bad label came from.

Restore pipelined successor pre-spawn and move the lazy-tester signal earlier in plan execution. Executor now sends `Task {N} code complete — writing impl report` to Lead *before* writing `impl.md` or committing; Lead lazy-spawns `tester-{N}` on that signal so the Tester cold-reads plan/product/testing docs in parallel with the Executor finishing the impl report. The same signal triggers pipeline pre-spawn: if a concurrency slot is free and there is a pending task whose only remaining blocker is task N, Lead pre-spawns that successor's Executor + Reviewer with a Pipeline-mode block in the spawn prompt. The pre-spawned Executor runs through steps 1–3.7 normally (codebase research, plan, Lead plan review) and then parks at a new step 3.9 wait gate, sending `Task {M} planning complete — awaiting implementation approval` to Lead. When the predecessor reaches `task done`, Lead sends `Implementation approved — predecessor task {N} passed all stages. Proceed to implement.` and the parked Executor runs 3.5/4/5/6 normally. At most one pre-spawn per `code complete` event; parked state is not persisted in checkpoints (pipeline is a latency optimization, not a correctness guarantee); on predecessor escalation the parked successor stays alive unless the user aborts. summary: Tmux layout daemon: replace break-pane/join-pane/resize-pane rearrangement with atomic select-layout. Each tick computes the target column layout, derives a TAILQ permutation via swap-pane (cheap pointer swaps, no layout re-flow), then applies a precomputed layout string (with layout_checksum reproduced in JS from tmux/layout-custom.c) in a single select-layout call. The whole arrange is one batched tmux invocation with exactly one redraw — sub-10ms regardless of pane count, effectively eliminating visible pane tearing. Daemon also sorts task-column members deterministically by role: executor (top), reviewer (middle), tester (bottom). Agents task-executor, code-review, and task-tester now self-label as `task-N-executor`, `task-N-reviewer`, `task-N-tester` respectively; legacy `task-N` labels (no role suffix) still classify correctly and sort after role-labeled siblings for backward compatibility. Replace label-based change detection with a target-layout signature so labeling a pane that doesn't change the resulting column assignment no longer triggers a redundant break-pane/join-pane cycle (reduces visible pane-tearing). Drop the post-arrange re-scan. Tighten poll interval from 2000ms to 1000ms for snappier reaction to new agent spawns.
